A Student-Centered Advocacy Campaign

From Awareness to Action:
Proper Waste Management

“Know the Right Thing. Do the Right Thing.”

About the Campaign

From Awareness to Action: Proper Waste Management is a student-centered campaign that encourages college students to turn what they already know about proper waste management into simple, consistent everyday actions. It promotes practical habits students can practice in school and at home: reducing waste, reusing materials, segregating trash, recycling, and disposing of waste properly.

The idea is simple: awareness is only the first step; action is what creates change. Instead of expecting big changes, the campaign invites students to start small with what they can control: disposing of their own trash properly, following segregation, cutting unnecessary waste, and keeping their own area clean.

The Problem

Many college students already know why proper waste management matters. However, awareness does not always turn into consistent action. Students may know that waste should be segregated, reduced, reused, recycled, and properly disposed of, yet these practices are not always followed in daily routines. This contributes to littering, improper waste disposal, and untidy classrooms and school surroundings.

This awareness–action gap is supported by Barloa, Lapie, and de la Cruz (2016), who surveyed 2,528 undergraduate students at Laguna State Polytechnic University – Los Baños Campus. Most students showed satisfactory knowledge and attitudes toward solid waste management, but fewer than half showed satisfactory practices.

73.4%satisfactory knowledge
71.0%satisfactory attitude
43.1%satisfactory practice

Knowing what to do does not always mean doing it. This campaign aims to close that gap by making proper waste management part of students’ everyday habits.

“You don’t have to do something big to help the environment. Start with your own waste, your own space, and your own actions.”
Our Advocacy

Small Actions, Cleaner Classrooms

Background and History

Proper waste management is a responsibility that begins with simple actions in everyday student life. In the Philippines, Republic Act No. 9003, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, promotes waste reduction, reuse, recycling, segregation, and proper disposal of solid waste. The law also stresses the importance of environmental awareness and education.

The campaign was developed on the belief that students can contribute through small, realistic actions. Rather than trying to solve the entire waste problem, it focuses on what students can personally control within their classroom, section, and school environment: disposing of personal waste properly, following segregation, reducing single-use materials, reusing items, and checking one’s area before leaving the room.

Goals and Objectives

General Goal

To encourage college students to turn their awareness of proper waste management into simple, consistent, and responsible daily actions.

Specific Objectives

  1. Increase awareness among students about basic waste management and waste segregation.
  2. Encourage students to properly dispose of their own waste after eating, studying, or joining classroom activities.
  3. Encourage students to reduce unnecessary waste, particularly single-use plastics and excessive paper use.
  4. Promote the reuse and recycling of materials whenever possible.
  5. Develop a simple “Clean Before You Leave” habit, where students check and clean their own area before leaving the classroom.
  6. Encourage students to be role models to their classmates by practicing proper waste management themselves.

The Everyday Actions

Four habits any student can start today, plus the one we practiced ourselves.

Dispose Properly: Our Own Photos

Campaign Flow

1 · Awareness

Introduce proper waste management through posters and a short class discussion.

2 · Action

Encourage students to practice proper disposal and segregation.

3 · Habit

Practice the “Clean Before You Leave” routine consistently.

4 · Result

A cleaner, more responsible classroom environment.

Campaign Materials

6. “Clean Before You Leave” Challenge
